item.title: 2026 Research Analyst
item.description: Work for the IMF. Work for the World. The Fund seeks dynamic and highly motivated Research Analysts (RAs) with strong quantitative and analytical skills. The successful candidates should have the proven ability to work independently, as well as collaboratively in a team environment. The RAs will be responsible for a wide range of support including, but not limited to, data gathering, econometrics, analysis of economic or statistical data sets, and basic programming for high-quality analyses. This is a contractual appointment for one year, renewable for up to four years of cumulative contractual service, depending on the business need and performance of the incumbent. Research Analyst positions are filled with candidates physically residing in the local Metropolitan Washington, D.C. area. Job Summary Supports departmental objectives on economic analysis and managing information technology & systems. Analyzes and computes statistical and economic data in support of the department. Additionally, the RA will manage Fund database(s) and contribute to staff reports. This opportunity may meet PREDOC requirements for applications to subsequent academic study. Major Duties and Responsibilities Compiles statistical data, compares and evaluates alternative data sources, and ensures consistency of series and definitions. Computes data collected using statistical and econometric techniques and develops summary analysis, including summary tables and charts for various reports. Develops and maintains comprehensive and fully documented cross-country databases in accordance with Fund-wide data management requirements on an ad-hoc basis. Maintains relevant computer software, and writes, updates, modifies, and executes computer programs for statistical and econometric analysis. Initiates analytical work, especially the econometric analysis, underpinning the work of relevant papers and publications produced by the work unit. Participates in divisional/departmental research projects and drafts targeted notes on selected issues of relevance to the division's /department’s work program. Participates in occasional departmental missions and liaises with country authorities, academia, or financial institutions. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Economics, Finance, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Data Science or other related quantitative field, but more competitive candidates would have a Master’s degree in the relevant field. Two years of relevant work experience in a similar role. Proficiency in MS Excel, including basic functions and formula. Proficiency in the use of analytical, statistical and econometric software packages such as STATA, EViews, R, TSP, SPSS, Matlab and SAS. Preferred: Experience working with finance, budget, people analytics, macroeconomic data and writing macroeconomic research reports. Experience and ability to use a range of visual presentation tools such as PowerPoint, MS Excel charts, Tableau, Keynote, Prezi and other similar tools. Familiarity with database management tools such as: Power BI, SQL, MS Access, IBM Cognos BI. Knowledge of Python, C++, and other similar programming tools would be a plus. In addition, the following competencies are critical to the position: Proven ability to manage large and complex databases and develop summary analysis, including summary tables and charts, and sound analytical and problem-solving skills, including a knowledge of statistical applications and techniques. Sound organizational and data management skills, and ability to handle several responsibilities and work under tight time constraints. Ability to work without direct supervision, paying close attention to details and bearing independent responsibility for data accuracy. Proven experience in dealing with all levels of staff in responding to a wide range of inquiries. Ability to use tact, discretion, and sound judgment when dealing with clients and in handling confidential information. Department: Hiring For: A06, A07, A08 The IMF is guided by the principle that the employment, classification, promotion, and assignment of staff shall be made without discrimination against any person. item.title: Research Analyst under the Research Analyst Program (RAP)
item.description: Work for the IMF. Work for the World. Work for the IMF. Work for the World. The Fund is currently seeking talented and motivated individuals with strong quantitative and analytical skills to join its Research Analyst Program (RAP). This program offers a unique opportunity for recent graduates to gain useful entry-level analyst experience and contribute to the IMF's important research and analytical projects before pursuing graduate studies. The RAP is limited to a two-year contractual period. All positions are located at the IMF Headquarters in downtown Washington, D.C. with Research Analysts in the RAP hired on a wide geographical basis. Job Summary As a RAP participant, you will contribute to, and support the operational and policy work of Fund economists. RAP participants may be asked to conduct research, collect and compile information, access and manipulate macroeconomic data from a wide range of sources. The RAP candidate will be expected to maintain and update economic, financial, and statistical databases, conduct quantitative data analysis utilizing econometric and other statistical tools, evaluate economic, financial or statistical relationships in databases, analyze economic time series data, and design systems to facilitate interfaces or to transfer data between external and in-house databases. As a research analyst, you will collaborate with economists and others on various projects and stay up to date with the latest developments in economics and related topics. This opportunity may meet PREDOC requirements for applications to subsequent academic study. Minimum Qualifications: •Recent completion of a bachelor's degree in economics, computer science, statistics, mathematics, finance, data science or other related quantitative field is required. Candidates with advanced degrees in the same relevant field may be considered with limited combined professional experience. •A cumulative GPA of at least 3.5/4.0 (or equivalent for international diplomas) in both the principal field of study and in the overall program. •Ability to work independently under minimum supervision and be accountable for the accuracy of both data and programs. •Proficiency in software applications such as Microsoft Office (specifically Excel and PowerPoint), econometric packages such as STATA, EViews, MATLAB and other statistical and analytical tools. •Knowledge of programming languages like Python and R are desirable. •Working knowledge of Tableau, familiarity with other data visualization tools, especially PowerBI, or Python/R based, or web design are desirable. •Strong analytical and quantitative skills. •Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. • Proficiency in other languages is a plus. Application Instructions: Applications from all geographical areas are welcome for the RAP. •Upload your unofficial/official transcript verifying your current/final GPA in your undergraduate studies along with your resume and cover letter in your application. Without uploading proof of GPA or an equivalent indication of academic achievement, your application may not be considered. •Note that only those identified for an assignment will be contacted to discuss their interest and availability by the hiring manager. item.title: Data and Modeling Analyst/Sr. Data and Modeling Analyst (Contractual) - ICDMF
item.description: Work for the IMF. Work for the World. The IMF's Institute for Capacity Development (ICD) seeks dynamic and highly motivated Data & Modeling Analysts (DMAs) with strong skills in data management, research design, and economic analysis. Successful candidates should have the proven ability to work independently, as well as collaboratively in a team environment. The DMAs will be responsible for a wide range of support including, but not limited to, data management and governance, data/technical implementation, and macroeconomic analysis and modeling, collaboration on software development, and providing support to country economists with the adoption of new software tools. Job Summary Supports the structuring, management, and governance of datasets underlying ICD's macroeconomic forecasting models, and the ongoing development and adoption of those modeling frameworks. Major Duties and Responsibilities Manage, structure, and maintain the databases and data pipelines underlying the macroframeworks software, ensuring data quality, integrity, and consistent documentation of data lineage. Establish and apply data governance standards — including data dictionaries, version control practices, and metadata documentation — in coordination with ICD's broader data management practices. Support Fund economists in creating, maintaining, and improving macroeconomic frameworks and models, updating databases and documentation. Support country teams with the adoption of the newly developed macroframeworks software, converting databases to a new system, helping with data cleanup and transformations. Support country teams in developing and linking macroeconomic models to the macroframework software, transferring models originally developed in Matlab (e.g. Dynare) or in Python environments, using basic programming techniques and internal solution tools. Contribute to refinements of the internal software package for macroframeworks and other related tools, by providing feedback, ideas, debugging, and collecting feedback from country desk teams. Liaise closely with the IT team on business requirement developments/updates, testing use cases from country teams and developer requests, and contributing to documentation updates. Minimum Qualifications Educational development, typically acquired through the completion of a university degree, or equivalent, in data managemet, programming/systems, computer science, statistics, finance, mathematics, economics, or a related field of study, is required. Experience and strong interest in macroeconomic modelling and forecasting. Relevant work experience in a similar role. Excellent data management and analytical skills, including experience with relational databases, data governance, and data quality assurance practices. Good knowledge of Python, R, or Matlab, and familiarity with SQL or other database query languages. Interest in or experience using large language models (LLMs) for code development. In addition, the following competencies are critical to the position: Strong spoken and written communication in English. Sound organizational and data management skills, and ability to handle several responsibilities and work under tight time constraints. Ability to work without direct supervision, paying close attention to details and bearing independent responsibility for accuracy. Proven experience in dealing with all levels of staff in responding to a wide range of inquiries. Ability to use tact, discretion, and sound judgment when dealing with clients and in handling confidential information. This is a one-year contractual appointment. Contractual appointments at the IMF are renewable for up to four years of cumulative contractual service, pending incumbent's performance, budget availability, and continuous business need. item.title: Resident Advisor in Financial Stability (SEETAC) (MCMTA)
item.description: Work for the IMF. Work for the World. The Monetary and Capital Markets Department (MCM) of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) is hiring an experienced and well-qualified expert to serve as Resident Advisor on financial stability at the Southeast Europe Technical Assistance Center (SEETAC). SEETAC—the IMF’s newest regional capacity development center (RCDC), dedicated to the Western Balkans and Moldova—will begin operations in January 2027. The Center will help member countries in the region—Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, and Serbia—strengthen their capacity to design and implement economic policies. SEETAC experts will deliver tailored, high-quality, and practical technical assistance (TA) and training in areas critical to sound macroeconomic management and in core areas of IMF expertise, including fiscal policy, monetary and financial sector policies, macroeconomic forecasting and policy, macroeconomic statistics, legal frameworks and institutions, and cross-cutting issues. The activity of the Center will be complemented by continued TA delivery from IMF HQ and training at the Joint Vienna Institute. This assignment is based in Rome, Italy, with an initial term of twelve months and the possibility of extension—typically for up to three to five years—based on performance and funding availability. Duties and Responsibilities: The Advisor will help strengthen capacity to assess and monitor systemic financial stability risks and further develop robust frameworks for macroprudential policymaking—two strategic objectives for the region. The Advisor will respond to capacity development (CD) requests from SEETAC members. The Advisor will assist the relevant authorities in developing and implementing well-prioritized medium-term CD work programs by: Supporting authorities in financial stability and macroprudential policy work, including financial sector risk analysis; monitoring and identification of systemic risks; compilation and selection of financial sector vulnerability and macroprudential indicators, and identification of related data gaps; implementation of macroprudential tools; development of decision-making structures and frameworks for macroprudential policy; macro stress testing, including scenario design and tool development; analysis of financial sector interconnectedness and shock transmission and amplification channels; and preparation and publication of financial stability reports that provide high-quality analysis and communicate risks clearly to the public. Managing and delivering TA on systemic risk analysis and macroprudential policies, directly and through short-term experts, who would be backstopped by the Resident Advisor. Preparing required documents for MCM internal review and approval before and after each mission and ensuring timely transmission of final documents to the relevant country authorities. Coordinating and delivering CD activities under SEETAC’s CD workplan on systemic risk analysis and macroprudential policies, directly and through short-term experts, including TA missions, training workshops, regional seminars, or peer-to-peer learning, tailored to the needs of CD recipient authorities. Keeping the MCM backstoppers informed of major developments. Coordinating with other CD providers on financial stability to promote complementarity, avoid duplication of efforts, and ensure efficient use of CD resources; liaising with donor representatives active in the field if needed. Observing IMF policies and procedures and applying the results-based management (RBM) framework to guide CD activities. The RBM framework focuses on performance and achievement results, supported by the Fund’s Capacity Development Management and Administration Program (CDMAP). Leading annual work planning and budgeting for SEETAC’s CD program on financial stability, contributing to outreach activities, and reporting on the Center’s activities. Ensuring that all advice is consistent with IMF policies. Qualifications The successful candidate should be able to demonstrate initiative and creativity and preferably have: At least ten years of experience working in a central bank on the operational implementation of macroprudential policies and systemic risk analysis. A graduate degree in economics, finance, or a related field. Strong oral and written communication skills in English. Strong drafting and reporting skills, with an ability to deliver high-quality CD outputs. Excellent interpersonal skills, including the ability to: (i) work effectively as part of a team, including with short-term experts and HQ staff; (ii) build effective relationships with CD recipient authorities, including senior government officials; and (iii) handle sensitive and confidential matters with discretion in a multicultural environment. Willingness, capacity, and commitment to undertake extensive travel within the region to support in-person CD delivery. Proficiency in modern computer systems and applications. Experience in delivering technical assistance, advisory services, capacity development, or professional training would be highly desirable. Compensation and benefits are competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience. Department: MCMTA Monetary and Capital Markets Dept. item.title: Resident Advisor in Central Bank Operations (SEETAC) (MCMTA)
item.description: Work for the IMF. Work for the World. The Monetary and Capital Markets Department (MCM) of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) is seeking an experienced expert to serve as Resident Advisor on Central Bank Operations at the Southeast Europe Technical Assistance Center (SEETAC). SEETAC—the IMF’s newest regional capacity development center (RCDC) for the Western Balkans and Moldova— will begin operations in January 2027. It will support member countries in the region—Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, and Serbia—strengthen their capacity to design and implement sound economic policies. SEETAC experts will deliver tailored, high-quality, and practical technical assistance (TA) and training in areas critical to sound macroeconomic management and in core areas of IMF expertise, including fiscal policy, monetary and financial sector policies, macroeconomic forecasting and policy, macroeconomic statistics, legal frameworks and institutions, and cross-cutting issues. The activity of the Center will be complemented by continued TA delivery from IMF HQ and training at the Joint Vienna Institute. This assignment is based in Rome, Italy, with a twelve‑month initial term and the possibility of extension—typically up to three to five years—based on performance and funding availability. Duties and Responsibilities The Resident Advisor will help support the continued modernization of central bank operations and governance across the region, tailoring advice to country-specific needs and responding to TA requests from SEETAC members. The Resident Advisor will help the authorities design and implement well-prioritized medium-term CD work programs by: Delivering TA on governance, accounting and central bank financial reporting, central bank communication and transparency, monetary policy implementation and domestic market operations, FX policy implementation, FX reserve management, and FX market development, and central bank liquidity backstops for financial stability, directly and through short-term experts backstopped by the Resident Advisor. Assessing monetary frameworks and advising on central bank operations in line with monetary policy regimes and the central bank mandates. Developing recommendations for legislative, regulatory, and operational reforms to improve monetary and foreign exchange market operations. Preparing documents for MCM and other Fund departments’ internal review and approval before and after missions and ensuring timely delivery of final outputs to country authorities. Coordinating and delivering CD activities under SEETAC’s CD workplan on central bank operations, including TA missions, regional workshops and seminars, and peer-to-peer learning, tailored to member countries’ needs. Keeping MCM backstoppers informed of key developments. Coordinating with other CD providers on central bank operations to promote complementarity, avoid duplication of efforts, and ensure efficient use of CD resources. Liaise with donor representatives active in the field if needed. Observing IMF policies and procedures and applying the results-based management (RBM) strategic framework to guide CD activities. The RBM framework focuses on performance and achievement results, supported by the Fund’s Capacity Development Management and Administration Program (CDMAP). Leading annual work planning and budgeting for SEETAC’s CD program on central bank operations, contributing to outreach activities, and reporting on the Center’s activities. Ensuring that all advice is consistent with IMF policies. Qualifications The successful candidate should demonstrate initiative and creativity and preferably have: At least five years of experience working in a central bank, in-depth understanding of international standards and good practices for monetary and foreign exchange market operations and experience of their implementation at the national and/or international level. A graduate degree in economics, finance, accounting, or a related field. Strong oral and written communication skills in English. Strong drafting and reporting skills, with an ability to deliver high-quality CD outputs. Excellent interpersonal skills, including the ability to: (i) work effectively as part of a team, including with short-term experts and HQ staff; (ii) build effective relationships with CD recipient authorities, including senior government officials; and (iii) handle sensitive and confidential matters with discretion in a multicultural environment. Willingness, capacity, and commitment to undertake extensive travel within the region to support in-person CD delivery. Proficiency in modern computer systems and applications, including AI. The successful candidate would be selected based on a written test and a panel interview. Compensation and benefits are competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience. Department: MCMTA Monetary and Capital Markets Dept. item.title: Resident Advisor in Monetary and Foreign Exchange Market Operations (CCAMTAC) (MCMTA)
item.description: Work for the IMF. Work for the World. The Monetary and Capital Markets (MCM) Department of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) is recruiting a well-qualified and experienced expert to work as resident advisor in monetary and foreign exchange market operations at the IMF Caucasus, Central Asia, and Mongolia Regional Capacity Development Center (CCAMTAC) located in Almaty, Kazakhstan. This is a twelve‑month initial assignment with the possibility of extension typically up to three to five years based on performance and funding availability. CCAMTAC is a multi-donor-financed Regional Capacity Development Center, providing capacity development (CD)—technical assistance (TA) and training—to nine member countries to strengthen their institutional capacity to design and implement sound macroeconomic and financial policies. The CCAMTAC member countries include Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyz Republic, Mongolia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. The resident advisor assists participating countries in modernizing their monetary policy frameworks and operations. Additionally, with the assistance of MCM and short-term experts, the resident advisor may be asked to provide support on other central bank operations. The advisor will be part of the CCAMTAC team ( https://ccamtac.imf.org/ ) and backstopped by the MCM Department of the IMF. Duties and responsibilities The resident advisor responds to CCAMTAC member countries’ CD and cooperation requests and is expected to travel or provide remote assistance to these countries to perform the assigned duties. The advisor is also expected to lead/organize selected training for the member countries in Almaty or in other locations. By elaborating well-prioritized medium-term work programs, s/he assists CCAMTAC members through: · Delivering TA on governance, accounting, and central bank financial reporting, central bank communication and transparency, monetary policy implementation and domestic market operations, FX policy implementation, FX reserve management, and FX market development, and central bank liquidity backstops for financial stability, directly and through short-term experts backstopped by the resident advisor. · Assessing monetary policy frameworks and advising on central bank operations in line with monetary policy regimes and the central bank mandates. · Developing specific recommendations on the necessary legislative, regulatory, and operational steps to improve monetary and foreign exchange market operations. · Preparing required documents prior to and after each mission for MCM internal review and approval and ensure transmission of final documents to the relevant country authorities. · Coordinating with MCM regarding member countries’ central bank operations TA requests . · Conducting, facilitating, or otherwise participating in country or regional workshops and seminars/ webinars on monetary and foreign exchange market operations, including collaborating with other resident advisors in CCAMTAC. · Coordinating with MCM, including backstoppers, on policy areas and keeping them up to date on major developments, to ensure that any advice provided by the advisor is consistent with IMF policies. · Observing IMF policies and procedures, applying the results-based management (RBM) strategic framework in guiding CD activities.[1] · Leading annual work planning and budgeting for the CD program in CCAMTAC on monetary and foreign exchange market operations and contributing to the Center’s reporting and outreach activities. Qualifications The successful candidate should demonstrate creativity and initiative and have: · At least five years of experience working in a central bank, in-depth understanding of international standards and good practices for monetary and foreign exchange market operations and experience of their implementation at national and/or international level. · Expertise in TA delivery in central bank operations is an advantage. · A graduate degree in economics, finance, accounting, or a related area. · Excellent interpersonal skills, including the ability to work effectively with senior policymakers in the region and the donor community, to lead teams of senior experts, to work as part of a team that would include staff at IMF headquarters as well as in CCAMTAC, and to handle sensitive and confidential issues with discretion in a multicultural environment. · Strong verbal and written communication skills in English, including presentational skills in support of training-related activities. · Good organizational and time management skills in balancing demands from member countries with duties and responsibilities from MCM and CCAMTAC. · Proficiency in modern computer systems and applications, including AI. The successful candidate will be selected based on a written test and a panel interview. Compensation and benefits are competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience. [1] The RBM framework focuses on performance and achievement results, supported by the Fund’s Capacity Development Management and Administration Program (CDMAP). item.title: Budget Officer - STARM
item.description: Work for the IMF. Work for the World. The Statistics Department (STA) has an opening for a Budget Officer in its Resource Management Division (STARM). STARM plays a central role in resource management and capacity development (CD) support for the Department, with responsibilities including: Managing, monitoring, and reporting on STA’s budget resources, including leading the preparation of the annual Medium-Term Budget (MTB) and accountability framework exercises. Coordinating STA’s CD activities through the Medium-Term Workplan (MTW). Obtaining and managing external funding for STA’s CD activities, in coordination with the Institute for Capacity Development (ICD). Providing logistical support for the recruitment and management of STA field experts. Advising staff and experts on the Fund’s travel policy and helping ensure procedures are applied consistently according to STA guidelines and Fund policies. Under the general supervision of the STARM Division Chief and working closely with STA’s Senior Budget Manager (SBM) and within a team environment, the successful candidate will contribute to the formulation of STA’s budget as well as the monitoring of its implementation and regular reporting to STA management. The incumbent is expected to contribute to STA’s resource planning and budgeting processes for CD and non-CD operations across the full range of funding sources (IMF01 and IMF02). The ideal candidate is a strong team player and a highly motivated self-starter with excellent judgment, who brings ownership, energy, a collaborative work style and innovation to their work, and who possesses strong knowledge of the IMF’s budget processes, policies and systems. Duties include: Contribute to the formulation of STA's MTB by compiling and analyzing budget-related data and forecasting future resource requirements including for personnel, travel, seminars, and other discretionary resources; Conduct technical analysis of budget requests and queries, and use sound judgment to make recommendations to the SBM and STA Management (when needed); Monitor the in-year implementation of STA’s budget, providing regular reports to the SBM on the projected year-end outturn, and support the budget team in preparing year-end accruals; Coordinate the monthly time-reporting submissions for STA and review for data accuracy and completeness; monitor and analyze divisions’ monthly reporting of donor chargebacks and project anticipated total fiscal year chargebacks; Conduct analyses of resource allocation and expenditures based on in-depth knowledge of the Fund’s budget policies and practices; provide suggestions for improvements to internal monitoring and forecasting systems; Work with OBP, FIN, ICD, HRD, ITD, and other stakeholders to enhance budgetary tools and work practices, such as the Capacity Development Management and Administration Program (CDMAP); Represent STA on interdepartmental committees and working groups on budget issues, as appropriate. Minimum qualification: Educational development, typically acquired by the completion of an advanced university degree, or equivalent, in business, finance, budgeting, accounting, statistics, computer science, or related field, or a Certified Public Accountant (CPA) or similar professional certification; or a university degree, or equivalent, supplemented by a minimum of six (6) years of relevant professional experience is required. Alternatively, a minimum of two (2) years of experience in a related position at Grade A8, or equivalent, is required. Additionally, the candidate is expected to have: Strong knowledge of the Fund's budget policies and procedures, both IMF01 and IMF02; Experience with Fund budget-related financial systems, and the ability to run queries in these systems; Excellent quantitative and analytical skills, including proficiency in Power BI, and Excel and its pivot function and ability to organize large quantities of data; Experience with the Fund’s new IT systems that impact the budget, including CDMAP and Workday; Demonstrated drive for results and ability to work proactively and independently, with limited supervision and as a member of a team; The ability to set priorities, work under pressure, and manage several tasks concurrently within tight deadlines while seeking innovation solutions to improve budget processes and outcomes; The ability to collaborate with staff at all grade levels both within and beyond STA; Proven competence in handling sensitive and highly confidential matters with discretion and diplomacy; Excellent interpersonal and relationship building skills; Strong oral and written communication competencies, as well as data visualization skills. The ability to learn new technologies and remain current with technology trends is essential (familiarity with AI-enabled tools, including responsible use and validation of outputs, to support analysis, drafting, and process improvement would be a plus).
